beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Naaman was a great man. Captain of the armies of Syria, honorable, mighty in valour. And under all that armor — he was a leper.

beats.text: In his house served a young girl carried captive out of Israel. She knew where healing was.

beats.text: So Naaman came — with his horses, his chariots, his silver and gold — and stood at the door of a plain little house. The prophet didn't even come out. He sent a messenger.

beats.text: Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

beats.text: And Naaman was furious. He had expected something great — a mighty ceremony worthy of a mighty man. It was too plain. Too simple. He turned and rode away in a rage.

beats.text: So the great captain went down, and dipped himself in the Jordan. Once. Twice. Seven times, exactly as the man of God had said.

beats.text: The instruction wasn't beneath him. It was the way back. If you've been away, the way back may look almost too simple — pray again, read again, come back again. Do the simple thing.
